candidates.title: YouVersion reveals what people searched for in the Bible this year
candidates.summary: The Bible App's yearly search data shows 'anxiety', 'hope' and 'healing' among the top searches, with 'Psalm 91' the single most-searched term. Daily use rose more than 13% to 18.5 million people, with 160M+ new installs in 2026. A November 30-Day Bible Challenge adds friend progress tracking.

candidates.title: Ascension introduces Catholic Reading Bible: Dyslexia-Friendly Edition
candidates.summary: The first complete Catholic Bible set in the Grace typeface by 2K/DENMARK, developed with input from dyslexic readers and researchers. It uses bottom-weighted letters, lines of no more than 35 characters, ragged-right text and colored reading overlays.
candidates.whyNotChosen: An accessibility design story that is narrower and print-based. Used as also-encouraging.

candidates.title: Pray.com opens its AI video studio to churches
candidates.summary: Pray Production Studio turns sermons into AI-generated cinematic videos using third-party video models, priced from $19 to $4,995 per month. Critics argue AI Bible videos turn Scripture into an action movie.
candidates.whyNotChosen: A commercial product launch built on a press release. Its best use is the honest-caution angle, so it is used for wisdomConcern.

candidates.title: Gloo AI Hackathon 2026 winners
candidates.summary: More than 1,000 builders on 115+ teams. The grand prize went to an agent for youth leaving foster care. The Best of Bible award (YouVersion) went to Envoy Mission, an offline, private Bible app shared through AI conversations with seekers.
candidates.whyNotChosen: The headline winner is a social-services tool, not a Christ-centered one. Only the Bible-category winner is in scope. Used as also-encouraging.

candidates.title: Music Bible app sets the entire Bible to AI-generated music in 11 styles
